context.firstUser: A teacher, streamer, coach, or group host who wants a fair random picker and needs paid unlimited access to be understandable, recoverable, and resistant to duplicate charges.
context.primaryJob: Recognize an existing plan, upgrade Monthly to Lifetime with one clear action, preserve Lifetime access, and recover a web purchase on another browser.
context.desiredResponse: The upgrade should feel simple and trustworthy: one dominant decision, exact renewal consequences, a protected recovery path, and an unmistakable next step if a previous subscription needs attention.
referenceProducts: Spin The Wheel — Random Picker — current random-picker category conventions and direct premium gating
Duolingo — clear plan-state recognition and high-visibility upgrade actions without losing product personality
Partiful — energetic consumer styling that keeps consequential actions legible and socially approachable

blurTest.evidence: The Lifetime headline, explanatory body, primary purchase or subscription-management action, secondary dismissal, and legal footer remain distinct visual masses on phone and tablet.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The upgrade and completion states use NameSnap's tactile lavender sheet, ink outline, violet depth, and warm action rather than a generic App Store paywall card.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: A Monthly owner immediately sees Make it Lifetime, a one-time $6.99 action, and an explicit explanation that the Apple subscription remains active until canceled.

realityTest.evidence: Rendered states use the actual Monthly and Lifetime products, exact prices, real App Store subscription-management destination, restore action, renewal consequences, and verified-email web recovery copy.

journeyTest.evidence: The monthly state leads directly to StoreKit Lifetime purchase; successful completion unlocks Lifetime and presents the subscription-management reminder without relocking the app. Web Monthly similarly exposes a single Lifetime upgrade path and blocks duplicate checkout.

platformTest.evidence: Original-resolution iPhone 17 Pro and iPad Pro 13-inch renders fit without clipping; native purchases remain StoreKit-native while web purchases use a verified passwordless purchase account and Stripe Checkout.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The UI explains what is owned, what Lifetime changes, whether another renewal can occur, how to restore access, and what to do if cancellation cannot be completed automatically.

implementationTest.evidence: The iOS simulator build, web lint, static production build, and Cloudflare Worker dry run succeed; server-side idempotency, account binding, duplicate-plan blocking, webhook verification, and subscription-cancellation fallback are implemented.

screenFindings.finding: The iPhone Monthly state has one dominant Lifetime purchase, no redundant Monthly option, complete renewal wording, restore access, and intact privacy and EULA links.
The iPhone completion state clearly separates completed Lifetime ownership from the remaining Apple subscription action and keeps the management button above dismissal.
The iPad paywall remains centered and compact, with its plan decision, consequence copy, and footer legible at tablet scale.
The iPad reminder preserves the same hierarchy and NameSnap component grammar without stretching the modal or hiding the underlying app context.
The web upgrade remains hidden until needed, fits on mobile, and now adds a secure passwordless purchase-account gate before either plan can open Checkout.
The repaired desktop stage preserves the dominant wheel and full control strip while paid status remains a secondary account action rather than squashing the live picker.

independentCritic.categoryFluency: PASS — plan ownership, one-time versus recurring price, restore, renewal management, and duplicate-charge prevention are all native to a paid utility.
independentCritic.originality: PASS — the purchase system uses NameSnap's established inked, hard-shadowed, lavender and warm-gold grammar instead of importing a generic SaaS checkout aesthetic.
independentCritic.marketingFrameLeakage: PASS — free use remains accountless and the payment UI appears only at the contestant limit or when an existing Monthly owner intentionally opens Lifetime upgrade.
independentCritic.importedCliches: PASS — trust is communicated through exact state and consequence text, not lock shields, bank-card hero art, or security theater.
independentCritic.adversarialFinding: The initial account resolver could have shown one purchaser's browser-bound entitlement after a different account signed in on the same shared browser. The resolver now refuses that cross-account fallback, and subscription webhooks preserve the bound account row.

repairs: Added explicit Monthly-versus-Lifetime entitlement state on iPhone and iPad and suppressed a second purchase of an already-owned plan.
Made the native Monthly-to-Lifetime action open StoreKit directly with one tap.
Added a post-purchase Apple subscription reminder because apps cannot cancel a customer's App Store subscription automatically.
Added passwordless verified-email purchase accounts to web while keeping all free picker use accountless.
Moved web Checkout Session creation behind the Worker, added Stripe idempotency and existing-session reuse, and blocked duplicate Monthly or Lifetime checkout per purchase account.
Added automatic Stripe Monthly cancellation after a successful web Lifetime upgrade plus a visible support fallback if cancellation fails.
Prevented entitlement crossover when different purchase accounts use the same browser.
verdict: PASS — the rendered native upgrade and post-purchase states, plus the compiled web purchase-account flow, meet the quality floor with no clipping, ambiguous ownership, redundant plan choice, or known same-account duplicate checkout path.
